title: May-to-June DMI change gave no clear added autumn forecast skill in 1981-2024
abstract: We tested whether the May-to-June change in the Indian Ocean Dipole Mode Index (DMI) adds autumn forecast skill beyond June DMI, June Nino 3.4 and a linear time trend. Expanding linear fits used earlier years from 1950. In 44 test years from 1981 to 2024, the added change reduced mean squared error by 0.15%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -2.18% to +3.09%. RMSE changed from 0.31764 to 0.31741 degrees C. Planned checks also gave intervals that include zero. The evidence gives no clear added skill for this feature and baseline. It does not show that ocean development has no physical effect. Revised inputs, a short test, a simple model and uncertainty conditional on fitted forecasts limit use. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and a figure are included. External raw data and record-level derivatives remain outside the baseline publication.

display.caption: Added DMI change gives no clear error reduction. Points are MSE reductions. Bars give conditional 95% paired block intervals. Positive values indicate smaller forecast error.

citations.reason: Prior level benchmark and trend check motivate the stronger baseline. Sources and test years overlap.
